name: Solomon Islands SWIM
summary: SWIM (Supporting Work in Ministry) is the CRCA's mission base in Honiara, Solomon Islands, offering Bible teaching, leadership training and practical support.

body.heading: What SWIM is
paragraphs: SWIM stands for Supporting Work in Ministry. It is a mission arm of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia, a Registered Charitable Trust in the Solomon Islands, and an associate member of the Solomon Islands Christian Association (SICA).
The Solomon Islands Workgroup (SIW) oversees SWIM for the CRCA. Board members visit the base, and CRCA churches and their members are SWIM's main supporters through prayer and giving.
SWIM's mission is: "Serving in Solomon Islands with compassion through Biblical teaching, equipping, and support in Jesus' name."

body.heading: Vision and values
paragraphs: SWIM's vision is: "As a mission community of Christ-centered people we will provide effective, practical, compassionate support and Bible based teaching and equipping ministries to build up Christians and establish self-reliant communities in Solomon Islands using our base facilities, resources, and the talents of our long and short term team members."
Eight biblical values shape all of SWIM's ministries: biblical teaching, unity, teamwork, godly leadership, loving people, prayer, spiritual growth and cultural relevance.

body.heading: What SWIM does
paragraphs: SWIM's work covers teaching and training church leaders, Know Your Bible (KYB), short-term mission teams, community development, practical aid and disaster relief, the Days for Girls program, school sponsorship, prison ministry, media ministry and support for the Bethesda Disability Centre.

Each week the base runs women's, children's, youth and sports ministries for the neighbouring communities, including Bible study, sewing lessons and the SWIM FC futsal team. SWIM's pastor, Michael Light, runs biblical leadership training at the base and in the provinces.

body.heading: Projects and partnerships
list: Crossroads prison ministry: Michael and Janet Light coordinate free Crossroad Bible Institute courses for inmates at Rove Correctional Centre. In 2026 the work grew to Tetere and Auki correctional centres. SWIM also gives release packs to inmates when they leave.

Bethesda Disability Centre: developed by SWIM with the Ministry of Health and People With Disabilities Solomon Islands (PWDSI). Since 2010 it has run three eight-week residential courses a year, teaching Christian faith, personal healthcare, gardening, woodwork and sewing. More staff houses are still needed.

Samasodu Village: over twelve years, SWIM partner teams built a Rural Health Centre and staff housing and improved sanitation and water supply. Australian teams are now building a high school. In July 2025 a team built a new girls' dormitory at Katova High School.
Water projects: at Kwainafala in North Malaita, a dam, two water tanks and 25 standpipes now serve 30 households.
School sponsorship: schooling in the Solomon Islands is not free or compulsory. Donations help pay tuition fees, school supplies and uniforms.

body.heading: The base
paragraphs: The base sits on a 5 acre block on the eastern outskirts of Honiara, about 12 km from the town centre and 4 km from the international airport. Long-term team members live and work in seven houses on the base. Power comes from solar panels backed by a generator, and water from rain catchment and a bore.

The Conference Centre and Transit House sleeps 34 people in bunk-style rooms, with a shared common room, dining area and kitchen. There is also a large leaf meeting house for conferences and workshops.
Short-term mission teams, retreats, conferences and workshops can book the base at very reasonable rates. Self-catering is usually required. Contact SWIM about bookings and rates.

items.title: Contact the SWIM Directors
items.text: Mission opportunities are those identified by SWIM's long-term missionaries. Talk with the SWIM Directors first and keep in touch with them while you plan.

items.title: Form your team
items.text: Teams should have no more than 10 people. Larger teams need permission from the SWIM Directors. Team leaders must be confessing Christians active in their local church, with a reference letter from their pastor.

items.title: Sign the agreement form
items.text: Every team leader and member signs the SWIM short-term mission agreement form, committing to SWIM's Christian values and principles.

items.title: Complete training before you go
items.text: All team members complete short-term mission training and orientation before the trip. SWIM provides training resources and recommends the 'Helping without Hurting in Short Term Missions' video study.

items.title: Serve alongside SWIM
items.text: Where possible, a SWIM missionary or staff member goes with the team. Teams follow the policy on conduct and dress, including no alcohol, betel nut or smoking.
